# Volume 2 — III Mr. Pettifer at Home

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

A thick grove of spruce backed the whitewashed, low-eaved, old-fashioned structure that was Mr. Pettifer’s house.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0000 }

In his shirt sleeves, Mr. Pettifer himself sat upon his vine-shaded veranda, taking pleasure in his pipe for the evening. As soon as he recognized the person approaching along the path, he leaped abruptly to his feet, darted inside the house, and closed the door. Although this was simply the awkward consequence of his astonishment, combined with a significant amount of shame regarding his fit of anger from the previous day, it almost completely robbed Nell of what little courage she had left in her heart.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0001 }

“If his temper is this bad already, how will he react upon learning my actions,” she pondered in despair while knocking on the door.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0002 }

However, Mr. Pettifer, displaying a sheepish smile, unfastened it and asked her to come inside using a voice that was rather anxious, yet completely gentle and amiable. Having put away his pipe and put on his jacket, he most courteously tendered Nell a seat covered in dust, and her greeting might have transpired agreeably enough were it not for the betrayer in the form of a parrot, who was gazing out from between the bars of his cage with malevolent yellow eyes. The moment Nell took her seat, Nutmeg cried,
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0003 }

“Goodness gracious, why is that red-haired slip of a girl heading over this way?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0004 }

Determining whether Mr. Pettifer’s or Nell’s face displayed the deeper shade of red would prove difficult.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0005 }

“Ignore that parrot,” Mr. Pettifer requested, glaring angrily at Nutmeg. “He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0006 }

“I ought to imagine so,” replied wretched Nell, her recollection of her mission suppressing her anger. It was clear that she was in no position to insult Mr. Pettifer given the situation. Once you had abruptly disposed of a person's Jersey cow without their awareness or permission, you had to accept his parrot echoing unflattering remarks. Even so, the “redheaded snippet” failed to display the complete submissiveness she might have shown under different conditions.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0007 }

“I’ve come to admit something to you, Mr. Pettifer,” she said with determination. “It’s . . . it’s regarding . . . that Jersey cow.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0008 }

“Bless my soul,” Mr. Pettifer nervously cried out, “did she go and force her way into my oats once more? Oh well, forget it . . . forget it if she did. It makes no difference . . . none whatever, I . . . I acted too hastily yesterday, that’s the truth. Forget it if she did.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0009 }

“Oh, if that were the only issue,” Nell sighed. “However, it is ten times more terrible. I do not . . .”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0010 }

“May God bless my soul, are you trying to tell me that she has wandered into the wheat I own?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0011 }

“No . . . no . . . it isn't the wheat. But . . .”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0012 }

“So it must be the cabbages! Has she gotten into the cabbages I was growing for the Exhibition, then?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0013 }

“The cabbages aren't the issue, Mr. Pettifer. I will disclose all . . . my purpose here was precisely that—however, I ask that you refrain from cutting in. My nerves are unsettled by it. Allow me to simply relate what happened without speaking a word until I have finished—after which you will surely have a lot to say,” was the ending Nell delivered, though merely in her mind.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0014 }

“I won’t say another word,” said Mr. Pettifer, and he kept his promise. Nutmeg, however, was under no agreement to remain quiet and continued to blurt out, “Redheaded snippet” every now and then, driving Nell almost out of her mind.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0015 }

“Yesterday, I locked my Jersey cow in our pen. I traveled to Delford this morning, and upon my return, I noticed a Jersey cow inside your oat field. Isolde and I drove her out, and it was unbelievably difficult. I was terribly soaked, exhausted, and annoyed—and right then, Mr. Shearer drove past and proposed purchasing the cow. Right then and there, I sold her to him for twenty dollars. My actions were improper. Naturally, I ought to have paused and discussed it with Thirza. However, I have a terrible habit of acting impulsively—anyone acquainted with me can confirm that. Mr. Shearer immediately led the cow off so she could be loaded onto the afternoon train.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0016 }

“Redheaded snippet,” Nutmeg repeated, her voice dripping with deep disdain.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0017 }

Then Mr. Pettifer stood up and, displaying a look that would have terrified any bird except a parrot, moved Nutmeg’s cage into a neighboring room and closed the door. Nutmeg screamed, used foul language, and generally behaved in a manner consistent with his reputation, but upon realizing he was alone, reverted to a moody silence.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0018 }

“Pardon me and continue,” Mr. Pettifer said as he resumed his seat. “That bird was never taught any manners by my brother the sailor.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0019 }

“I returned to my house, and once I had finished my tea, I walked out toward the milking pen. Mr. Pettifer,” . . . Nell bent her body forward, interlacing her fingers in her accustomed youthful manner, as her large gray eyes stared pleadingly directly at Mr. Pettifer’s uncomfortable face . . . “I discovered that my cow was still locked inside the pen. The cow I had sold to Mr. Shearer belonged to you.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0020 }

“Bless my soul,” cried Mr. Pettifer, utterly astonished by this unexpected ending. “What a very extraordinary thing!”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0021 }

“Oh, my causing trouble for myself and everyone else is not at all surprising,” Nell stated in a sorrowful manner. “That is what I am known for. One would think I would have outgrown such behavior at my age . . . I turn seventeen this coming March . . . yet it appears I still have not. Mr. Pettifer, can I dare to ask for your forgiveness? Returning your cow is no longer possible, I fear, but this money will pay for her . . . or if you prefer, you may take mine as a replacement. My cow is an excellent one. And my regret over everything that happened is beyond words.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0022 }

“Tut, tut,” Mr. Pettifer said smartly, “miss, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur. On occasion, I am overly impetuous myself, miss . . . much too impetuous. However, I am unable to refrain from voicing my exact thoughts, and people are required to accept me as I am. Now, had that cow gotten into my cabbages . . . yet do not dwell on it, she did not, hence everything is fine. Because you wish to dispose of her, I believe I would prefer taking your cow in trade.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0023 }

“Ah, my gratitude, Mr. Pettifer. It brings me great joy that you feel no annoyance, as I feared it would upset you.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0024 }

“And I imagine you were terrified to come over here and inform me, given the scene I caused yesterday, right? However, you must not pay me any attention, as I am merely a terribly candid old man . . . extremely prone to stating what is real, even when it happens to be somewhat direct.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0025 }

“Mrs. Sowerby is too,” Nell remarked, blurting it out before she could stop herself.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0026 }

“Who? Mrs. Sowerby? Do not tell me that I resemble that ancient chatterbox,” Mr. Pettifer said in an annoyed manner. “I am not . . . not in the least. What is inside that box?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0027 }

“A cake,” Nell stated playfulnessly. Her mood rose as light as a feather due to her relief regarding the unpredicted friendliness of Mr. Pettifer. “I brought it over for you . . . I thought perhaps you didn’t have cake very often.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0028 }

“I do not, indeed, and I am extremely pleased with it, as well. You have my gratitude. The surface appears nice. My expectation is that it remains just as nice underneath.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0029 }

“It is,” Nell remarked, filled with cheerful certainty. “In the past, I have baked cakes that were not, which Mrs. Wace could confirm for you, yet this particular one is perfectly fine. Although I baked it for the Improvement Society, I am able to bake them another one.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0030 }

“Listen to my suggestion, young lady, you need to assist me in consuming it. After I set the kettle to boil, a cup of tea will be enjoyed by both of us. Is that acceptable to you?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0031 }

“Would you allow me to prepare the tea?” Nell asked uncertainly.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0032 }

A laugh came softly from Mr. Pettifer.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0033 }

“It appears you lack faith in my tea-making skills. You are mistaken . . . the pot of tea I can make is as fine as any you have ever tasted. However, you may proceed on your own. Luckily, Sunday brought rain, meaning clean dishes are available in abundance.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0034 }

Leaping up nimbly, Nell got to work. Prior to putting the tea to steep, she rinsed the teapot through a number of waters. Next she swept the stove and laid the table, fetching the dishes from inside the pantry. Although the condition of that pantry appalled Nell, she prudently kept quiet. Mr. Pettifer directed her to the place where the bread and butter and a tin of peaches were kept. Nell decorated the table using a flower arrangement gathered from the garden and ignored the spots on the tablecloth. Before long, the tea had brewed, and Nell was seated across from Mr. Pettifer at his personal table, serving his tea, and conversing openly with him regarding her school, companions, and intentions. The reality of her experience seemed almost unbelievable to her.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0035 }

Nutmeg was returned by Mr. Pettifer, who declared that the unfortunate bird would become lonely; whereupon Nell, convinced that she was able to pardon all people and all things, extended a walnut to him. Nevertheless, Nutmeg suffered from deeply wounded emotions and spurned every attempt at reconciliation. Perched disconsolately, he puffed out his plumage to such a degree that he resembled nothing more than a sphere of gold and green.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0036 }

“Why do you call him Nutmeg?” inquired Nell, who favored fitting names and believed Nutmeg did not suit such magnificent feathers in the least.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0037 }

“It was my brother, the sailor, who gave him his name, perhaps as an allusion to the way he behaves. Nevertheless, I hold that bird in high regard . . . you would hardly believe how deeply attached to him I am. Naturally, he is not without his flaws, and in various ways, he has proved quite expensive for me. A few individuals dislike the fact that he curses, yet the habit is impossible to cure, despite my own efforts and those of others. Certain people harbor a dislike for parrots, which seems foolish, doesn't it? As for me, I am fond of them, and Nutmeg provides me with a great deal of companionship. Not a single thing on this earth could persuade me to part with him . . . absolutely nothing, miss.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0038 }

Mr. Pettifer hurled the final sentence toward Nell with such explosive force that he might have thought she possessed a secret intention to convince him to relinquish Nutmeg. Nell, nonetheless, was starting to grow fond of the peculiar, anxious, restless small man, and prior to the conclusion of the meal, they had become rather good friends. Mr. Pettifer learned of the Improvement Society and felt inclined to view it favorably.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0039 }

“That is correct. Proceed. Ample space exists for progress within this colony . . . as well as among its inhabitants.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0040 }

“Oh, I don’t know,” Nell snapped back. In her own mind, or when speaking with her closest friends, she could concede that Brierley and the folks living there possessed a few minor flaws that could be readily fixed. However, listening to a virtual stranger such as Mr. Pettifer express that view was a completely different matter. “I think Brierley is a lovely place; and the people in it are very nice, too.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0041 }

“It seems you possess a bit of a temper,” remarked Mr. Pettifer, observing the red cheeks and angry eyes across from him. “I suppose that accompanies hair of your shade. Brierley is quite a nice location or I would not have settled here; however, I assume even you will agree it possesses a few shortcomings?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0042 }

“I prefer it all the more because of them,” answered faithful Nell. “I do not care for places or folk that do not possess any flaws. It seems to me that an entirely flawless individual would be extremely dull. Mrs. Milton White mentions that she has not encountered a flawless individual herself, though she has listened to plenty regarding one . . . the initial wife of her husband. Is it not your opinion that living as the spouse of a man whose initial wife possessed no flaws would be quite unpleasant?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0043 }

“To be wedded to the flawless wife would prove even more unpleasant,” Mr. Pettifer announced, displaying an abrupt and unexplainable intensity.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0044 }

After they finished tea, Nell made a point of doing the dishes, even though Mr. Pettifer gave her his word that the house contained sufficient crockery to last for weeks to come. She would have been delighted to sweep the floor as well, but because no broom could be seen, she refrained from asking about its location out of concern that one did not exist.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0045 }

“You could come over and speak with me now and then,” proposed Mr. Pettifer as she was departing. “The distance isn't great and people should show neighborliness. I feel a bit intrigued by that society of yours. It appears to me that it will offer some amusement. Which person will you approach first?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0046 }

“It is only places we mean to improve . . . we are not going to meddle with people,” Nell stated, adopting a dignified tone. That Mr. Pettifer was mocking the endeavor was her sneaking suspicion.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0047 }

After her departure, Mr. Pettifer observed her through the windowpane . . . a supple, youthful figure, stepping buoyantly over the meadows amid the evening twilight.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0048 }

“I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap,” he spoken out loud, “but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0049 }

“Redheaded snippet,” rasped Nutmeg in a taunting manner.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0050 }

Mr. Pettifer brandished his fist toward the parrot.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0051 }

“You stubborn creature,” he grumbled, “I nearly wish I had broken your neck back when my brother the sailor carried you to our house. Are you ever going to stop causing me difficulties?”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0052 }

Nell rushed back to her house cheerfully and described her experiences to Thirza, who had felt quite anxious because she had been away for so long and was just about to go search for her.
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0053 }

“Taking everything into account, this world is actually rather nice, wouldn’t you say, Thirza?” Nell cheerfully remarked. “A few days ago, Mrs. Sowerby was grumbling about how disappointing the world is. According to her, any pleasant anticipation inevitably ends in some degree of letdown . . . maybe she has a point. Even so, there is a positive aspect as well. Dismal anticipations also fail to materialize as terribly as expected . . . almost invariably, the reality proves far superior to one's fears. My trip to Mr. Pettifer’s house this evening was something I anticipated with utter dread; yet he proved to be rather gentle, making the visit almost enjoyable. Provided we show each other great tolerance, I believe genuine friendship lies ahead for us, and the entire situation has resolved most favorably. Even so, Thirza, I am positive that I will never dispose of a cow again without first confirming her rightful owner. Furthermore, parrots are not to my liking!”
{: #nw-v02-c03-p0054 }
